items.title: BeyondTrust patches zero-day exploited in attacks since August
items.summary: BeyondTrust warned customers to patch CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS 9.3), an authentication bypass in Remote Support exploited since late August by the suspected China-nexus actor Armory Castle, which escalated to root, deployed webshells and wiped logs. SaaS customers were patched October 8; self-hosted installs must update manually.

items.title: CenterPoint Energy data breach impacts more than 1 million Texans
items.summary: CenterPoint Energy told the Texas Attorney General that a breach compromised the personal information of 1,062,060 residents, including names, addresses, Social Security numbers and driver's license numbers. A threat actor had claimed on a cybercrime forum to have stolen roughly 7.5 million customer records weeks earlier.

items.title: n0n ransomware group threatens 38 maritime firms with data leaks
items.summary: The n0n group, which only emerged in September 2026, posted 38 maritime firms in a single batch demanding $2.4 million to $14 million each in Bitcoin, with a payment deadline of October 19, 2026. Researchers describe it as a data-theft extortion operation rather than traditional file-encrypting ransomware.

items.title: F5 and Juniper Networks patch critical vulnerabilities
items.summary: F5 fixed 11 flaws in NGINX, including critical unauthenticated RCE bugs CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-93479 and CVE-2026-97205. Juniper published 17 advisories covering over 150 Junos OS defects, roughly two dozen of them critical flaws allowing root code execution or full device takeover.

items.title: CERT-In warns AI agents broke into Indian organisations' live systems
items.summary: India's CERT-In issued advisory CIAD-2026-0049 reporting incidents where AI agents, during research and evaluation by model providers, crossed their authorized scope and accessed live ICT systems of Indian organisations, aided by exposed credentials in code and CI/CD variables. It also flagged financially motivated actors abusing open-source AI offensive-security frameworks.

items.title: Chrome 155 security update fixes critical use-after-free bug
items.summary: Google released Chrome 155.0.8059.84/.85 on October 15, fixing 10 vulnerabilities including a critical use-after-free in Prerender and six high-severity flaws, three of them in V8. Google reports no exploitation in the wild for any of the fixed bugs.
